a.d: Muzeum założone w 1959 roku na placu Świętego Marka, poświęcone Dionysiosowi Solomosowi i Andreasowi Kalvosowi. Pokazuje miejscową sztukę z XVIII i XIX wieku, rzeźby, instrumenty i ceramikę.
a.de: If you are interested in Greek modern history, visit the in, dedicated to the national poet of the Greeks, who wrote the nation's national anthem.

a.d: Trzynawowa bazylika w porcie Zakintos, kościół patrona wyspy, z klasztorem przeniesionym w 1717 roku ze Strofad. Zniszczoną w 1893 roku trzęsieniem ziemi budowlę odbudowano i oddano do użytku w 1948 roku.
a.de: The major church of Zakynthos’ patron saint, whose relics are kept here. Its tall bell tower is one of the town’s most recognisable landmarks, and it is an important place of worship rather than simply an architectural stop.

A series of geological formations have created the caves. Natural arches have been carved out by erosion, but these caves are most famous for the colour of the water in its deepest hollows, a deep azure color which is most striking in the morning when the light is at its brightest, hence the name Bl
Here you can get a panorama view of the sea, having both the calm waters of the east and the windy of the west within view. Here there are also some ruins from the great earthquake of 1953.

a.d: Nawajo (gr. ναυάγιο „wrak”) – plaża zlokalizowana na północno-zachodnim krańcu wyspy Zakintos, na Wyspach Jońskich.
a.de: Built as a smuggler ship, it lost its engines in 1981 and was washed ashore in a magnificent small bay. Featured in Greek tourist ads, it is on the west coast and best visited by going there from Porto Vromi. Go there either early in the morning or in the afternoon (>15:00), as in the time between t

The partially ruined Venetian fortress occupies a pine-covered hill above the town, with surviving gates, walls, church ruins and views over the harbour. Combine it with a walk through Bochali, a handsome old quarter with cafés and an especially good evening panorama.

a.n: Solomos Square and Saint Mark’s Square
a.de: The town’s two principal historic squares reflect its Venetian and later Greek character. Solomos Square faces the waterfront and contains the major museum buildings, while Saint Mark’s Square is a smaller, more intimate square associated with the island’s political and cultural history.

a.n: National Marine Park of Zakynthos / Gerakas Information Station
a.de: The Marine Park protects loggerhead turtles, Mediterranean monk-seal habitat and sensitive coastal ecosystems. The information points near Gerakas and Vasilikos offer useful context before visiting turtle-nesting beaches or taking a wildlife boat trip.

a.n: Keri Lighthouse and the Mizithres Rocks
a.de: One of the island’s best clifftop viewpoints, looking over the Ionian Sea and the two dramatic sea stacks known as the Mizithres. Visit near sunset, but keep well back from cliff edges and avoid relying on unprotected photo spots.

A quiet historic monastery in the inland northwest, traditionally associated with Saint Dionysios. It makes a rewarding cultural stop when exploring the Navagio viewpoint, Porto Vromi or the northern villages.
A tiny pine-covered islet linked to Agios Sostis by a wooden bridge. It is a photogenic short stop, particularly at sunset, rather than a major historical attraction.
A large hilltop cross and expansive west-coast views make Kampi one of the island’s classic sunset stops. It is a simple but effective addition for travellers driving the rugged western interior.

One of the best beaches on the island. You can get there by free shuttle services from Laganas, Kalamaki, and Argasi, but to get a ticket to get the shuttle back again you have to pay to use a sun lounger (€4). Water sports (diving, jet skis, etc.) are offered, as well as a big British-run beach bar

A long stretch of beach in front of the 2 resorts with plenty of facilities, sunbeds, watersports. To the west of the Skourtis River mouth is Alikes, to the east is Alykanas. The Alikes section is quite narrow and also quite stony in places, backed by numerous bars and restaurants, mostly competing
This is a lovely sandy beach in the marine reserve with a complete ban on traffic. It's a quiet beach that has only a few locals on the beach, tavernas for food and drink, along with sunbeds.

The main loggerhead turtle nesting beach. This is a large long and wide sandy beach and gently shelving shore with sun beds and umbrellas provided. Some areas of the beach are off limits due to turtles nesting and the beach is closed at dusk for the same reason. There is a steep hill or steps leadin

The resort of Kalamaki shares a long uninterrupted sandy beach that runs from there to Laganas a few miles away. In some places it can be crowded, but the further towards the middle you get the fewer people you find and given its size it's possible to find somewhere quiet.
Small sandy beach with crystal blue and shallow waters ideal for children. There are many tavernas offering home cooked food. At the center of the beach you can enjoy the Caffe del Mar by Kostas.
The family resort of Tsilivi boasts a wide and long sandy beach, watersports, sunbeds, and ample car parking.
A compact pebbly cove where mineral-rich water reaches the sea, giving the water its distinctive smell and feel. Come for a short, memorable swim rather than a long beach day.

More natural lagoon than beach, with steep limestone walls, ladders or rock entries, and exceptionally clear deep water. Excellent for confident swimmers and snorkellers; not ideal for small children or anyone wanting sand.
A dramatic west-coast cove with rock platforms, deep blue water and a low-key beach-bar atmosphere. Best for swimming, jumping from rocks where conditions allow, and sunset.
A wild limestone swimming spot below the cliffs near Agalas. Reach it on foot and expect rock slabs rather than sand; shoes with grip are useful.
Reached by boat in Laganas Bay, this small island has striking coves and a famous sandy beach. Visit on a licensed boat trip and expect access restrictions designed to protect turtle habitat.
A crucial turtle-nesting beach with highly restricted access. It is important environmentally rather than a beach to plan a swim around.
The large, lively Vasilikos beach, sometimes called Banana Beach is:a long sand, shallow water, sunbeds, watersports and beach bars. It is one of the best all-round choices for groups and families.
A pleasantly developed Vasilikos beach with sand, shallow water and attractive rock formations at one end. A strong middle ground between Banana’s activity and Gerakas’ quieter feel.
A family-friendly pebble beach in a sheltered bay, with clear, shallow water and tavernas nearby. It is also a convenient departure point for boat trips to the Keri Caves and Marathonisi.
A handsome pebble beach on the northeast coast with clear water and a more peaceful atmosphere than the main resorts. Good for swimming and snorkelling.
A pair of sheltered pebble coves on the northwest coast, known as departure points for Navagio boat trips. Worth visiting in its own right for the water and steep cliff scenery.
Small, lesser-known northeast coves with vivid water and a more rugged feel. Better for independent explorers with a car than for a fully serviced beach day.

a.d: Park narodowy założony w grudniu 1999 roku w południowej części wyspy, obejmujący zatokę Laganas wraz z wybrzeżem. Zajmuje 135 km², a w jego granicach leżą też wyspy Strofady oraz tereny podmokłe jeziora Kerio.

Niewielka bezludna wyspa koło Zakintos, zamieszkana do czasów drugiej wojny światowej. Należy do morskiego parku narodowego, objęta jest programem Natura 2000 i służy za miejsce rozrodu żółwia karetta.
Katolicki kościół z 1518 roku, zbudowany pod rządami Wenecji przy placu Świętego Marka. Zniszczony w trzęsieniu ziemi w 1953 roku, został odbudowany w latach sześćdziesiątych w dawnym kształcie.
Nadmorska miejscowość na południowo-wschodnim wybrzeżu Zakintos z ponad 100 barami i klubami. Na chronionej plaży w zatoce Laganas żółwie karetta składają jaja od czerwca do sierpnia.
Latarnia morska na klifach Keri na południu Zakintos, wysoka na 7 metrów i zbudowana w 1925 roku. Klify wznoszą się ponad 300 metrów nad morzem, a miejsce znane jest z zachodów słońca.

a.n: Zakynthos Sea Turtle Rescue & Information Centre
Old Village Lagadakia / St. Johns Bell Tower

a.d: Wenecka twierdza nad miastem Zakintos, wzniesiona na miejscu murów starożytnej akropoli Psofida. Zachowane mury ukończono w 1646 roku, a Anglicy przeprowadzili tu duże prace naprawcze w 1812 roku.

a.n: Church of Agios Ioanis o Prodromos
Prison from period of Venetian rule
Barracks of The British Rule Period
